memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting and take off the linen garments he put on before he entered the Most Holy Place, and he is to leave them there. He shall bathe himself with water in the sanctuary area and put on his regular garments. Then he shall come out and sacrifice the burnt offering for himself and the burnt offering for the people, to make atonement for himself and for the people." - Lev 16:23-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The linen is left behind. Aaron washes, puts on his ordinary priestly garments, and comes back out.

There is something moving in this. The clothes he wore into God's presence stay in the holy place. He does not carry them into normal life. But he does not stop being a priest either — he changes into his regular garments and keeps serving.

Many of us struggle with the transition between spiritual heights and ordinary days. A wonderful time of worship on Sunday, and then Monday morning arrives with its emails and its traffic and its short temper. The mountain-top experience fades, and we wonder whether it was real.

Peter wanted to build shelters on the mountain of transfiguration and stay (Matt 17:4). Jesus led them back down, and at the bottom of the hill was a desperate father with a suffering son.

The linen stays in the holy place. But the man who wore it comes out changed, and does his ordinary work as someone who has been in God's presence.

You cannot live on the mountain. You are meant to come down carrying what happened there.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you struggle when spiritual highs fade into ordinary days?
2. What have you carried out of God's presence into your everyday life?
3. How can Monday be shaped by what happens on Sunday?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the moments when I sense Your presence closely. Help me carry what You give me there into the ordinary days, and serve You faithfully in them. Amen.
